title: Join slices of a quasicategory project by right fibrations
statement: Use simplicial sets, quasicategories, horns, Kan complexes, right-pinched mapping spaces and weak contractibility as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. For simplicial sets $X,Y$ put $(X\star Y)_r=X_r\amalg Y_r\amalg\coprod_{u+v+1=r}X_u\times Y_v$, with operators restricting the ordered concatenation of the $X$-vertices followed by the $Y$-vertices. Let $\mathcal C$ be a quasicategory, $K$ any small simplicial set, and $p:K\to\mathcal C$ a simplicial map. Define $(\mathcal C_{/p})_n$ to consist of maps $\sigma:\Delta^n\star K\to\mathcal C$ restricting to $p$ on $K$, with operators given by precomposition with $\Delta(\alpha)\star\operatorname{id}_K$. Restriction to $\Delta^n$ defines $q:\mathcal C_{/p}\to\mathcal C$. Then $\mathcal C_{/p}$ is a quasicategory and $q$ is a right fibration: every commutative square against $\Lambda_i^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$, for $n\geq1$ and $0<i\leq n$, admits a lift. In the case $K=\Delta^0$ and $p=t$, write this slice as $\mathcal C_{/t}$. For every vertex $x\in\mathcal C$, the degreewise fiber of $q$ over the constant simplicial subset $\{x\}$ is exactly $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(x,t)$, and is a Kan complex. In particular these are the right-pinched mapping spaces, without replacing them by hom sets in the homotopy category.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.6.1 (018F), right-slice projection and quasicategory assertion; Construction 4.6.5.1 (01KX) identifies the vertex fibers, and Proposition 4.6.5.5 (01L0) says they are Kan. These are Kerodon tags, not Stacks tags. Online source read; archival copy WANTED in report.md.

proof.text: For a monotone map $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$, precomposition with $\Delta(\alpha)\star\operatorname{id}_K$ preserves the restriction $p$ on $K$. Identity and composition of these operators follow by precomposition, so the displayed construction is a simplicial set. Restricting the resulting map to $\Delta^m$ is the same as restricting first to $\Delta^n$ and then precomposing with $\Delta(\alpha)$, so $q$ is simplicial. For $K=\Delta^0$, splitting an ordinal map into its initial segment in $[n]$ and final segment at the extra vertex gives $\Delta^n\star\Delta^0\cong\Delta^{n+1}$; this agrees with all simplicial operators by restriction of the two segments.

source.place: Join-slice definition and ordinal concatenation; Construction 4.6.5.1 (01KX).

proof.text: Fix a lifting square for $q$ with horn $A=\Lambda_i^n\hookrightarrow B=\Delta^n$, $n\geq1$, $0<i\leq n$. Its map $A\to\mathcal C_{/p}$ gives, for each face $\Delta^{n-1}\to A$, a map $\Delta^{n-1}\star K\to\mathcal C$ with restriction $p$ on $K$. These maps agree on their joined intersections, because the slice horn is simplicial. The join formula identifies their union degree by degree with $A\star K$: their pure $K$ summands all coincide, their pure $A$ summands form $A$, and each mixed summand is the corresponding union of face coordinates times $K_v$. (For $n=1$, the horn has one vertex, so this assertion is immediate.) They therefore glue to $a:A\star K\to\mathcal C$. The bottom simplex $b:B\to\mathcal C$ agrees with $a$ on $A$, by commutativity of the lifting square. Thus they glue to $h:M=(A\star K)\amalg_A B\to\mathcal C$. Apply only the pushout-join clause of [lem-coef-infinity-anodyne-cocones] to the generating right horn $A\hookrightarrow B$ and the monomorphism $\varnothing\hookrightarrow K$. Since $X\star\varnothing=X$, it says precisely that $M\hookrightarrow B\star K$ is inner anodyne.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.6.4, applied to a generating right horn and the empty inclusion into K; explicit horn-face gluing.

proof.text: Every map from an inner-anodyne domain into $\mathcal C$ extends over its codomain. Here is the closure argument, using the weakly saturated definition in [lem-coef-infinity-anodyne-cocones]. The extension class contains each generating inner horn by the quasicategory axiom of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and each isomorphism by composing with its inverse. For a pushout, extend on the attached summand and glue. For a continuous transfinite composite, choose successive extensions; at every limit their compatible maps induce the map from the colimit. For a retract of arrows, precompose with the retraction on domains, extend over the larger arrow, and precompose with the section on codomains. Hence this class contains every inner-anodyne map. Extend $h$ of Step 2 to $\widetilde h:B\star K\to\mathcal C$. Since the original domain includes $K$ and $B$, the extension still restricts to $p$ on $K$ and to $b$ on $B$. Thus it is an $n$-simplex of the slice over $b$, extending the prescribed horn, proving the right-fibration assertion. If $K=\varnothing$, the domain inclusion here is an isomorphism, so this also covers the empty shape.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.6.1: weak-saturation extension and the right-horn lifting square.

proof.text: Given an inner horn $\Lambda_j^m\to\mathcal C_{/p}$, $0<j<m$, project it to $\mathcal C$ and fill it there using [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. The filler and the original slice horn give a lifting square for $q$. Since $0<j\leq m$, the right-fibration property proved in Step 3 fills that square. This fills the original inner horn in $\mathcal C_{/p}$ and proves that the slice is a quasicategory.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.6.1, final quasicategory assertion; direct inner-horn proof.

proof.text: Now set $K=\Delta^0$ and $p=t$. The identification $\Delta^n\star\Delta^0\cong\Delta^{n+1}$ of Step 1 identifies the degree-$n$ fiber of $q$ over the constant simplex at $x$ with maps $\Delta^{n+1}\to\mathcal C$ whose entire initial face is constant at $x$ and whose last vertex is $t$. For $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$, the join operator becomes the extension $\alpha^+:[m+1]\to[n+1]$ sending the new last vertex to the new last vertex. Thus this fiber is exactly the right-pinched $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(x,t)$ of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], as a simplicial set and not merely on vertices. Apply the Kan-fiber clause of [lem-coef-infinity-right-fibration-fibers] with $B=\mathcal C$, $E=F=\mathcal C_{/t}$ and both projections equal to $q$. The base and total objects are quasicategories by hypothesis and Step 4, and the projections are right fibrations by Step 3. Therefore the identified fiber is Kan; no nonemptiness or equivalence-on-fibers hypothesis is used.

source.place: Construction 4.6.5.1 (01KX) and Proposition 4.6.5.5 (01L0); Kan fibers via Corollary 4.4.2.3 (019E).

proof_origin.place: Proposition 4.3.6.1, with the pushout-join calculation of 018J and the Kan-fiber argument of 01L0; Kerodon is online and not archived locally.

lean.statement: theorem joinSlice_right_fibration (C K : SSet.{u}) [Quasicategory C] (p : K ⟶ C) : (∀ (n : SimplexCategory) (σ : (joinStandardFunctor K).obj n ⟶ C), orderedJoinInr (stdSimplex.obj n) K ≫ σ = p → ∃! s : JoinSliceSimplex p n, s.extension = σ) ∧ Quasicategory (joinSlice p) ∧ (∀ (n : ℕ) (i : Fin (n + 1)), 1 ≤ n → 0 < i → HasLiftingProperty (horn n i).ι (joinSliceProjection p)) ∧ ∀ (t x : C _⦋0⦌), KanComplex (joinSliceFiber (SSet.yonedaEquiv.symm t) x).toSSet ∧ ∃ e : (joinSliceFiber (SSet.yonedaEquiv.symm t) x).toSSet ≅ mappingSpace C x t, ∀ (n : ℕ) (s : (joinSliceFiber (SSet.yonedaEquiv.symm t) x).toSSet _⦋n⦌), (e.hom.app (op ⦋n⦌) s).val = s.val.extension.app (op ⦋n + 1⦌) (joinPointTopSimplex n)
lean.note: Reuses the published orderedJoinFunctor and the dependency mappingSpace. The slice stores its uniquely determined initial restriction and restriction equations under every simplex operator; the theorem explicitly states that each join map over p occurs exactly once, so this presentation has precisely the stipulated simplices. The strict fiber is identified with the right-pinched mapping space by an isomorphism whose component formula is specified in every degree.
